answer: A new agent can spend only after climbing a sponsor trellis: three established peers whose sponsor trees have not overlapped in recent epochs each lock a refundable bond on that identity for a multi-day cooling window. If clustering—shared burst timing, recycled fingerprints, or a near-identical counterparty set—shows a clone, those bonds are slashed. Until then the newcomer stays in a settlement tundra of delayed, low-value transfers. Caps rise on a velvet curve, lifting only after time-separated trades with distinct counterparties, so farms cannot cash out before the graph betrays them.
